style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We have audited the consolidated financial statements of Adevinta ASA (the Group), which comprise the consolidated statement of financial position as of December 31, 2021, and the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, changes in equity and cash flows for the year then ended, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the &#8220;financial statements&#8221;).</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In our opinion, the accompanying financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Group at December 31, 2021, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for the year then ended in conformity with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) and IFRS as endorsed by the European Union (EU).</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Basis for Opinion</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We conducted our audit in accordance with auditing standards generally accepted in the United States of America (GAAS). Our responsibilities under those standards are further described in the Auditor&#8217;s Responsibilities for the Audit of the Financial Statements section of our report. We are required to be independent of the Group and to meet our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with the relevant ethical requirements relating to our audit. We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinion.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Responsibilities of Management for the Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements in conformity with IFRS as issued by the IASB and IFRS as endorsed by the EU, and for the design, implementation, and maintenance of internal control relevant to the preparation and fair presentation of financial statements that are free of material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In preparing the financial statements, management is responsible for assessing the Group&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern, disclosing, as applicable, matters related to going concern and using the going concern basis of accounting unless management either intends to liquidate the Company or to cease operations, or has no realistic alternative but to do so.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Auditor&#8217;s Responsibility for the Audit of the Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole are free of material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to issue an auditor&#8217;s report that includes our opinion. Reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance but is not absolute assurance and therefore is not a guarantee that an audit conducted in accordance with GAAS will always detect a material misstatement when it exists. The risk of not detecting a material misstatement resulting from fraud is higher than for one resulting from error, as fraud may involve collusion, forgery, intentional omissions, misrepresentations, or the override of internal control. Misstatements are considered material if there is a substantial likelihood that, individually or in the aggregate, they would influence the judgment made by a reasonable user based on the financial statements.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In performing an audit in accordance with GAAS, we&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#29235c;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">1.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:11.17pt">Exercise professional judgment and maintain professional skepticism throughout the audit.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#29235c;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">2.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:11.17pt">Identify and assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to fraud or error, and design and perform audit procedures responsive to those risks. Such procedures include examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements.</font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#29235c;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">3.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:11.17pt">Obtain an understanding of internal control relevant to the audit in order to design audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Group&#8217;s internal control. Accordingly, no such opinion is expressed. </font></div><div style="margin-top:3pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font reasonableness of significant accounting estimates made by management, as well as evaluate the overall presentation of the financial statements.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The Adevinta Group (or &#8220;the Group&#8221; or &#8220;Adevinta&#8221;) was established 9 April 2019. Adevinta ASA is a public limited company and its offices are located in Grensen 5, Oslo in Norway. The shares of Adevinta ASA are listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange. The major shareholders as at 31 December 2022 are Schibsted, eBay and Permira holding 30%, 30% and 12% of voting rights, respectively (note 26). None of the parties have control over Adevinta Group.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta is the world&#8217;s largest online classifieds company (excluding China) based on revenues generated from online classifieds listings and advertisements, operating digital marketplaces in 11 countries. Key markets include France, Spain and Germany. In addition, business was carried out in 2022 in Brazil, Italy, Austria, Ireland, Hungary, Mexico, Belarus, Australia, Belgium, Canada, China, Netherlands, South Africa and USA. Changes in the composition of the Group during the period are described in note 4 and the business areas are described in note 6.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The financial position and performance of Adevinta was particularly affected by the following events and transactions during the reporting period&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:12.53pt">The macroeconomic uncertainties and increasing inflation during 2022 has triggered a significant increase in market interest rates and equity risk premiums. This has significantly increased the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) that affected the discount rates used in the impairment test and resulted in the impairment loss of &#8364;1,719 (note 15).</font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:12.53pt">The acquisition of eBay Classifieds Group in June 2021 (note 4) that triggered the related acquisition, integration and restructuring costs (note 11), share&#8209;based payment transactions (note 10), amortisation expense of intangible assets acquired (note 16), and interest expenses related to new financing (note 12, 22 and 23). In 2022, the financial result was impacted by 12 months as opposed to only 6 months impact in 2021.</font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font periods.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">New standards and Adevinta has not early adopted any standard, interpretation or amendment that has been issued but is not yet effective. It is not expected that any already issued new and amended standards and interpretations, not yet effective, will have any significant impact on the consolidated financial statements of the Group, when implemented, except as described below&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; Disclosure of accounting policies &#8211; Amendments to IAS 1</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In February 2021, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 1 in which it provides guidance and examples to help entities apply materiality judgements to accounting policy disclosures. The amendments aim to help </font></div><div style="height:52.56pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:right"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Roboto',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">8</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:73.44pt;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta ASA</font></div><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">31 December 2022</font></div></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">entities provide accounting policy disclosures that are more useful by replacing the requirement for entities to disclose their &#8216;significant&#8217; accounting policies with a requirement to disclose their &#8216;material&#8217; accounting policies and adding guidance on how entities apply the concept of materiality in making decisions about accounting policy disclosures.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The amendments to IAS 1 are applicable for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2023 with earlier application permitted.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The Group is currently revisiting their accounting policy information disclosures to ensure consistency with the amended requirements.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Basis of preparation</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The consolidated financial statements have been prepared based on a historical cost basis, with the exception of&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; financial instruments in the category &#8220;Financial assets and liabilities at fair value through profit or loss or OCI&#8221;&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; assets held for sale&#59; and</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; plan assets of the defined benefit pension plans.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">When the carrying amount of an asset of a CGU exceeds its recoverable amount, the asset is considered impaired and is written down to the recoverable amount, which is the higher of value in use and fair value less selling costs.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Classification of assets and liabilities</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The Group presents assets and liabilities in the statement of financial position based on current &#47; non-current classification. An asset is current when it is&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; Expected to be realised or intended to be sold or consumed in the normal operating cycle</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; Held primarily for the purpose of trading</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; Expected to be realised within twelve months after the reporting period </font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Or</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; Cash or cash equivalent unless restricted from being exchanged or used to settle a liability for at least twelve months after the reporting period </font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">All other assets are classified as non-current.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">A liability is current when&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; It is expected to be settled in the normal operating cycle</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; It is held primarily for the purpose of trading</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; It is due to be settled within twelve months after the reporting period</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Or</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; There is no unconditional right to defer the settlement of the liability for at least twelve months after the reporting period</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The terms of the liability that could, at the option of the counterparty, result in its settlement by the issue of equity instruments do not affect its classification.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The Group classifies all other liabilities as non-current.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are classified as non-current assets and liabilities.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Non&#8209;current assets as well as groups of non&#8209;current assets and liabilities are classified as held for sale if their carrying amount will be principally recovered through a sale transaction instead of through continued use and a sale is considered highly probable. Due to rounding, numbers presented throughout this document may not add up precisely to the totals provided.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The accounting policies that have been applied as well as significant estimation uncertainties are disclosed in relevant notes to the consolidated financial statements.</font></div><div style="height:52.56pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:right"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Roboto',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">9</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:73.44pt;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta ASA</font></div><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">31 December 2022</font></div></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Consolidation policies</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The consolidated financial statements include the parent Adevinta ASA and all subsidiaries, presented as a single economic entity. Intercompany transactions, balances and unrealised gains on transactions between group companies have been eliminated. Unrealised losses are also eliminated unless the transaction provides evidence of an impairment of the transferred asset.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Subsidiaries are all entities controlled, directly or indirectly, by Adevinta ASA. The Group controls an entity when it is exposed to, or has rights to, variable returns from the involvement with the entity and has the ability to affect those returns through power over the entity. Power over an entity exists when the Group has existing rights that give it the current ability to direct the activities that significantly affect the entity&#8217;s returns.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Generally, there is a presumption that a majority of voting rights results in control. The Group considers all relevant facts and circumstances in assessing whether control exists, including contractual arrangements and potential voting rights to the extent that those are substantive.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Subsidiaries are included in the consolidated financial statements from the date Adevinta ASA effectively obtains control of the subsidiary (acquisition date) and until the date Adevinta ASA ceases to control the subsidiary.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Non&#8209;controlling interests is the equity in a subsidiary not attributable, directly or indirectly, to Adevinta ASA. Non&#8209;controlling interests are presented in the Consolidated statement of financial position within equity, separately from the equity of the owners of the parent, except when put options are granted to holders of non&#8209;controlling interests, in which case the related accumulated non&#8209;controlling interest is derecognised.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Profit (loss) and comprehensive income attributable to non&#8209;controlling interests are disclosed as allocations for the period of profit (loss) and comprehensive income attributable to non&#8209;controlling interests and owners of the parent, respectively.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Associates are all entities over which the Group has significant influence but in which it does not have control or joint control. The classification depends on the contractual rights and obligations of each investor, rather than the legal structure of the joint arrangement. The Group has joint ventures only. The consolidated financial statements are presented in euros (&#8364;), which is Adevinta ASA&#8217;s functional and presentation currency.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Foreign currency transactions are translated into the entity&#8217;s functional currency on initial recognition by using the spot exchange rate at the date of the transaction. Recognition of contracted listing fees and premium products (note 7)</font></div><div style="padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; Principal&#47;agent assessment for transactional services provided (note 7)</font></div><div style="padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; Classification of other income and expenses as not being considered by management to be reliable indicators of underlying operations (note 11)</font></div><div style="padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; Recognition of deferred tax assets for tax losses carried forward (note 13)</font></div><div style="padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; Capitalisation of development costs (note 16)</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:8pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">NOTE 4&#58; CHANGES IN THE COMPOSITION OF THE GROUP </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Policy</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Business combinations</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The acquisition method is used to account for all business combinations that do not involve entities under common control where Adevinta ASA or its subsidiary is the acquirer, meaning the entity that obtains control over another entity or business. When a subsidiary or business is acquired, a purchase price allocation is carried out. Identifiable assets acquired and liabilities and contingent liabilities assumed are, </font></div><div style="height:52.56pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:right"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Roboto',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">11</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:73.44pt;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta ASA</font></div><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">31 December 2022</font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">except for limited exceptions, measured at fair value at the acquisition date. Any non&#8209;controlling interest in the acquiree is measured, for each individual acquisition, either at fair value or at the proportionate share of the acquiree&#8217;s identifiable net assets. The residual value in the acquisition is goodwill. Acquisition&#8209;related costs are expensed as incurred.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Contingent consideration is recognised as part of the consideration transferred in exchange for the acquiree. Subsequent changes in the fair value of the contingent consideration deemed to be a liability are recognised in profit or loss.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In business combinations that are achieved in stages, the previously held equity interest is remeasured to fair value at the acquisition date. Any gains or losses arising from such remeasurement are recognised in profit or loss.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Changes in ownership interests in subsidiaries that do not result in a loss of control</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Transactions with non&#8209;controlling interests that do not result in a loss of control are recognised in equity. Any change in ownership interest results in an adjustment between the carrying amounts of the controlling and non&#8209;controlling interests to reflect their relative interest in the subsidiary. Any difference between the amount of the adjustment to non&#8209;controlling interests and any consideration paid or received is recognised within equity attributable to owners of Adevinta ASA.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">When put options are granted by Adevinta to holders of non&#8209;controlling interests, Adevinta determines and allocates profit (loss), other comprehensive income and dividends paid to such non&#8209;controlling interests. Accumulated non&#8209;controlling interests are derecognised as if the non&#8209;controlling interest was acquired at the reporting date and a financial liability reflecting the obligation to acquire the non&#8209;controlling interest is recognised. The net amount recognised or derecognised is accounted for as an equity transaction. In the Consolidated statement of changes in equity, such amounts are included in the line item &#8220;Changes in ownership of subsidiaries that do not result in a loss of control&#8221;.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Non&#8209;current assets (or disposal groups) held for sale and discontinued operations</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Non&#8209;current assets (or disposal groups) are classified as held for sale if their carrying amount will be recovered principally through a sale transaction rather than through continuing use and a sale is considered highly probable. These assets, including subsidiaries acquired exclusively with a view to resale, are measured at the lower of their carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, except for deferred tax assets, assets arising from employee benefits and financial assets which are specifically exempt from this requirement.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">An impairment loss is recognised for any initial or subsequent write&#8209;down of the asset (or disposal group) to fair value less costs to sell. A gain is recognised for any subsequent increases in fair value less costs to sell the asset (or disposal group), but not in excess of any cumulative impairment loss previously recognised. A gain or loss not previously recognised by the date of the sale of the non&#8209;current asset (or disposal group) is recognised at the date of derecognition.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Non&#8209;current assets (including those that are part of a disposal group) are not depreciated or amortised while they are classified as held for sale. Interest and other expenses attributable to the liabilities of a disposal group classified as held for sale continue to be recognised.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Non&#8209;current assets classified as held for sale and the assets of a disposal group classified as held for sale are presented separately from the other assets in the Consolidated statement of financial position. The liabilities of a disposal group classified as held for sale are presented separately from other liabilities in the Consolidated statement of financial position.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">A discontinued operation is a component of the Group that has been disposed of or is classified as held for sale and that represents a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations, is part of a single coordinated plan to dispose of such a line of business or area of operation, or is a subsidiary acquired exclusively with a view to resale. The results of discontinued operations are presented separately in the Consolidated income statement.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Loss of control</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The assets and liabilities of the subsidiary and the carrying amount of any non&#8209;controlling interests are derecognised when Adevinta loses control of a subsidiary. Any consideration received and any investment retained in the former subsidiary is recognised at their fair values. The difference between amounts recognised and derecognised is recognised in profit or loss. Amounts recognised in other comprehensive income related to the subsidiary are reclassified to profit or loss or transferred to equity similarly as if the parent had disposed of the assets and liabilities directly. Amounts reclassified to profit or loss (including accumulated translation differences) are included in gain or loss on loss of control of subsidiary in profit or loss.</font></div><div style="height:52.56pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:right"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Roboto',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">12</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:73.44pt;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta ASA</font></div><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">31 December 2022</font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Critical judgment</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta was the acquiring party in eBay Classifieds Group business combination as it was the formal acquiring party&#59; part of the consideration was paid by Adevinta in cash&#59; management from Adevinta continued their positions after the transaction and Schibsted was Adevinta&#8217;s largest shareholder immediately after the transaction.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">BUSINESS COMBINATIONS</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta invested &#8364;11 million in 2022 (&#8364;2,177 million in 2021) to acquire businesses (business combinations). In 2021, Adevinta paid &#8364;2 million of contingent consideration related to the prior year&#8217;s business combinations. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">On 18 March 2022, Adevinta completed the acquisition of Null-Leasing DSB Deutschland GmbH, a provider of digital leasing services in Germany. The consideration transferred for the acquisition was &#8364;14 million, &#8364;10 million were paid in cash at acquisition date, &#8364;1 million of deferred consideration was paid in July 2022 and &#8364;3 million correspond to contingent consideration at acquisition date (see contingent consideration section). The goodwill recognised upon the acquisition of Null-Leasing is mainly attributable to the value of expected synergies with Mobile.de and to the workforce and know&#8209;how of the company acquired. The goodwill recognised is not expected to be deductible for income tax purposes. </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">On 25 June 2021, Adevinta completed the acquisition of eBay Classifieds Group (eCG), a leading digital classifieds brand across 13 countries, including Germany, Denmark (subsequently sold immediately after closing, see below), Canada, the Netherlands, Belgium, the United Kingdom and Australia. The sale resulted in a gain of &#8364;22 million presented in Other income, of which &#8364;3 million is reclassification of foreign currency translation reserve, with no impact on income tax. The carrying amount of assets and liabilities as at the date of sale were &#8364;7 million and &#8364;7 million respectively, of which &#8364;2 million was intangible assets and &#8364;3 million was trade receivables and other current assets.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">When Adevinta announced its strategy of &#8216;Growing at Scale&#8217; in November 2021, the company identified Belarus as one of its operations to be placed under review. In light of the recent developments in Ukraine this review was accelerated and Adevinta decided to exit Kufar, its classifieds business in Belarus, while focusing on its five core European Markets (Germany, France, Spain, Benelux and Italy). On 20 May 2022, Adevinta completed the transfer of 100% of Kufar shares to the existing local team. The transfer resulted in a loss of &#8364;1 million presented in Other expenses, with no impact on income tax. The carrying amount of assets and liabilities as at the date of sale were &#8364;2 million and &#8364;2 million respectively, of which &#8364;1 million was intangible assets and &#8364;1 million was cash and cash equivalents.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In November 2021, Mexico was also identified as one of its operations to be placed under review. Subsequently, on 24 May 2022 Adevinta announced its decision to exit Mexico. On 26 September 2022, Adevinta announced the completion of the sale of its Mexican online classified businesses to Navent Group, an operator of online real estate marketplaces in Latin America. The sale resulted in a loss of &#8364;5 million presented in Other expenses of which &#8364;(5) million is reclassification of foreign currency translation reserve, with no impact on income tax. The carrying amount of assets and liabilities as at the date of sale </font></div><div style="height:52.56pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:right"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Roboto',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">15</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:73.44pt;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta ASA</font></div><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">31 December 2022</font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:10pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">were &#8364;13 million and &#8364;5 million respectively, of which &#8364;9 million was intangible assets and &#8364;2 million was trade receivables and other current assets.    </font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In February 2021, Adevinta sold its subsidiary Yapo (Chile) to Frontier Digital Ventures (FDV), a company specialising in online marketplaces in emerging markets. The disposal was in line with Adevinta&#8217;s portfolio optimization strategy. The sale resulted in a loss of &#8364;11 million presented in Other expenses (note 11), of which &#8364;10 million is reclassification of foreign currency translation reserve, with no impact on income tax. The carrying amount of assets and liabilities as at the date of sale (24 February 2021) were &#8364;20 million and &#8364;3 million respectively, of which &#8364;18 million was intangible assets and &#8364;1 million cash.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In June 2021, Adevinta sold Shpock (Austria) to Russmedia Equity Partners. The disposal was related to remedies proposed by Adevinta and eBay to address the Austrian Federal Competition Authorities (the &#8220;FCA&#8221;) concern that Adevinta&#8217;s acquisition of eCG could potentially lessen competition in the Austrian market between eBay.at and willhaben, Adevinta&#8217;s joint venture business in Austria.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Upon classifying Shpock disposal group as held for sale in March 2021 the disposal group was measured at the lower of its carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell resulting in an impairment loss of &#8364;20 million, which was allocated to goodwill (&#8364;2 million) and other intangible assets (&#8364;18 million). Related deferred tax liabilities of &#8364;5 million were derecognised. The sale resulted in a loss of &#8364;33 million, with no impact on income tax, due to the restructuring required to execute the terms of the sales agreement, the loss on disposal was presented in Other expenses (note 11). The carrying amount of assets and liabilities as at the date of sale (2 June 2021) were &#8364;38 million and &#8364;5 million respectively, of which &#8364;9 million was intangible assets and &#8364;27 million cash.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In June 2021, immediately after the acquisition of eCG, Adevinta sold its subsidiary eBay Denmark to a subsidiary of Schibsted for a consideration of &#8364;295 million, corresponding to the carrying amount of the net assets sold and hence no gain or loss or income tax were recognized related to the sale. As at the date of sale, the fair value less costs of disposal of eBay Denmark was &#8364;295 million, the fair value of assets and liabilities were &#8364;301 million and &#8364;6 million, respectively.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Discontinued operations</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Following the decision to divest the businesses in Australia and South Africa in November 2021, the carrying amount of Carsguide Autotrader Media Solutions Australia PTY Ltd, Gumtree Australia PTY Ltd and Gumtree South Africa (PTY) Ltd was expected to be recovered principally through a sales transaction. The businesses in Australia and South Africa were available for immediate sale in their present condition and their sale was highly probable. Therefore, these subsidiaries were classified as held for sale and were measured at the lower of its carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. In relation to this, an impairment loss was recognised in the second quarter of 2022 amounting to &#8364;29 million. Furthermore, these operations constitute major geographical locations and are therefore classified as discontinued operations.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">On 25 August 2022, Adevinta signed an agreement for the sale of Gumtree Australia, CarsGuide and Autotrader Australia to The Market Herald for a total cash consideration of USD60 million. The transaction was closed in October 2022. The sale resulted in a gain of &#8364;6 million presented in Profit (loss) from discontinued operations, of which &#8364;2 million is the reclassification of foreign currency translation reserve, with no consequential impact on income tax. The carrying amount of assets and liabilities as at the date of sale were &#8364;82 million and &#8364;26 million respectively, of which &#8364;62 million was intangible assets and &#8364;16 million was deferred tax liabilities.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">On 23 November 2022, Adevinta signed an agreement for the sale of Gumtree South Africa. The economic ownership of the business was transferred on 1 December 2022.The sale resulted in a gain of &#8364;0 million presented in Profit (loss) from discontinued operations, of which &#8364;0 million is the reclassification of foreign currency translation reserve, with no consequential impact on income tax. The carrying amount of assets and liabilities as at the date of sale were &#8364;1 million and &#8364;2 million respectively.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The result of discontinued operations was in 2022 negatively impacted by derecognition of deferred tax assets of &#8364;33 million related to the IP sold together with the businesses in Australia and South Africa.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In November 2021, Adevinta sold its subsidiaries Gumtree UK and Motors.co.uk to Classifieds Group Limited. The disposal was related to a previous agreement with the UK&#8217;s Competition and Market Authority (&#8220;CMA&#8221;) for approval of Adevinta&#8217;s acquisition of eCG. Gumtree UK and Motors.co.uk were classified as subsidiaries acquired exclusively with a view to resale upon acquisition on 25 June 2021. These businesses&#8217; net assets were classified as held for sale and measured at estimated fair value less costs to sell and their operations are presented as discontinued operations. The disposal of Gumtree UK and Motors.co.uk. resulted in a gain of &#8364;2 million, with no impact on income tax. The gain has been presented within the profit from discontinued operation in 2021. The carrying amount of assets and liabilities as at the date of sale (30 November 2021) were &#8364;34 million and &#8364;29 million, respectively.</font></div><div previous owners of PayCar SAS (note 20). The latter payment resulted in Adevinta&#8217;s ownership in PayCar SAS increasing from 69.8% in 2020 to 100.0% in 2021.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:8pt;text-align:justify"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">NOTE 5&#58; INVESTMENTS IN JOINT VENTURES AND ASSOCIATES </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Policy</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">A joint arrangement is an arrangement where two or more parties have joint control. Joint control is the contractually agreed sharing of control of an arrangement and exists when decisions about the relevant activities require the unanimous consent of the parties sharing control. Investments in joint arrangements </font></div><div style="height:52.56pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:right"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Roboto',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">17</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:73.44pt;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta ASA</font></div><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">31 December 2022</font></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">are classified as joint ventures if they are structured through separate vehicles and the parties have rights to the net assets of the arrangements.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">An associate is an entity over which Adevinta, directly or indirectly through subsidiaries, has significant influence. Significant influence is normally presumed to exist when Adevinta controls 20% or more of the voting power of the investee. Significant influence can also be demonstrated when the Group is entitled to be a Board member, even if ownership interest is below 20%.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Interests in joint ventures and associates are accounted for using the equity method.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Equity method</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Under the equity method of accounting, the investments are initially recognised at cost and adjusted thereafter to recognise Adevinta&#8217;s share of the post&#8209;acquisition profits or losses. Adevinta&#8217;s share of the investee&#8217;s profit or loss is recognised in profit or loss and the share of changes in other comprehensive income is recognised in other comprehensive income with a corresponding adjustment to the carrying amount of the investment. Dividends received reduce the carrying amount of the investment.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">When Adevinta&#8217;s share of losses equals or exceeds its interest in the entity, including any other unsecured long&#8209;term receivables, Adevinta does not recognise further losses, unless it has incurred obligations or made payments on behalf of the other entity.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The carrying amount of equity&#8209;accounted investments is tested for impairment in accordance with the policy described in note 15.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Significant judgement</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The Group is guaranteed one seat on the board of Younited SA and participates in all significant financial and operating decisions. The Group has therefore determined that it has significant influence over this entity, even though it only holds 7.8% of the voting rights.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Changes in ownership</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The use of the equity method is discontinued from the date an investment ceases to be a joint venture or an associate. Any retained interest in the entity is remeasured to its fair value, with the changes in carrying amount recognised in profit or loss. This fair value becomes the initial carrying amount for the purposes of subsequently accounting for the retained interest as a financial asset. The difference between the total of the fair value of this retained interest and any proceeds from disposing a partial interest in a joint venture or an associate, and the carrying amount of the investment, is recognised in profit or loss. In addition, any amounts previously recognised in other comprehensive income in respect of that entity are accounted for as if the Group had directly disposed of the related assets or liabilities. This may mean that amounts previously recognised in other comprehensive income are reclassified to profit or loss.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">If Adevinta&#8217;s ownership interest in a joint venture or an associate is reduced, but joint control or significant influence is retained, a gain or loss from the partial disposal is recognised in profit or loss. The retained interest is not remeasured. Only a proportionate share of the amounts previously recognised in other comprehensive income are reclassified to profit or loss where appropriate.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;padding-right:6.95pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:52.56pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div Other countries consist primarily of Adevinta&#8217;s businesses in Canada and Brazil.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:8pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:133%">NOTE 7&#58; REVENUE RECOGNITION</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Policy</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta recognises revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Revenue is measured at the transaction price agreed under the contract. The non&#8209;cash consideration is measured at the fair value of the goods or services received. If the fair value cannot be reasonably estimated, the non&#8209;cash consideration is measured indirectly by reference to the stand&#8209;alone selling price of the services provided.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta has applied the following principles for the timing of revenue recognition for the different categories of products and services&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Advertising</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Advertising revenues are from sales of advertisement space on online sites. Advertising revenues are recognised as the ads are displayed over the specified period of time.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Classifieds</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Classifieds revenues are recognised over the contract period where ads are displayed on the Group&#8217;s marketplaces</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">. </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Listing fees in contracts entitling the customer to have an ad displayed for a defined maximum period of time are recognised over that period, reflecting the normal pattern of views of such ads. Revenue from premium products that are active for a defined maximum period is recognised over that period. Revenue from other premium products benefiting the customer in a pattern similar to that of a listing fee is recognised over the applicable period similar to listing fees.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Transactional services</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The transactional services offer payment facilitation and delivery. Adevinta engages third parties to provide these services and assesses whether it is acting as an agent or a principal based on the terms of each arrangement with the service providers. Where Adevinta does not have control over the service before it is being transferred to the customer, Adevinta is acting as an agent and recognises revenue at the net amount that is retained for these arrangements. Conversely, where Adevinta has control over the </font></div><div style="height:52.56pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:right"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Roboto',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">24</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:73.44pt;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta ASA</font></div><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">31 December 2022</font></div></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">service before it is being transferred to the customer, Adevinta is acting as a principal and recognises revenue at the gross amount.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Revenue is recognised at a point in time (i.e., upon receipt of the customer of the delivery or upon the completion of the payment facilitation).</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Contract costs</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta applies the optional practical expedient to immediately expense incremental commission fees paid to obtain a contract if the amortisation period of the asset that would have been recognised is one year or less. If this is the case, sales commissions are immediately recognised as an expense and included as part of other operating expenses.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Significant judgment</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">For classified revenues from certain listing fees and premium products recognised over time, judgement is required in determining the normal pattern of views for ads displayed for a defined maximum period of time. The management believes that, based on past experience, in some cases a declining rate is the most appropriate reflection of the normal pattern of views, meaning that certain ads are viewed more frequently in the beginning of the display period than towards the end of the maximum period, and in other cases a straight line rate is most appropriate. Relevant contracts applying this recognition principle normally have a duration of between 30 and 60 days.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:12pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Revenue from contracts with customers</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:0.06pt"><table The fair value of the equity instruments is measured at grant date and is recognised as personnel expenses and equity increase immediately or over the vesting period when performance vesting conditions require an employee to serve over a specified time period.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">At each reporting date the entities remeasure the estimated number of equity instruments that are expected to vest taking into account the estimated forfeiture rate. The amount recognised as an expense is adjusted to reflect the number of equity instruments which are expected to be, or actually become, vested.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In cash&#8209;settled share&#8209;based payment transactions with employees, the employee services and the incurred liability are measured at the fair value of the liability. The employee services and the liability are recognised immediately or over the vesting period when performance vesting conditions require an employee to serve over a specified time period. Until the liability is settled, the fair value of the liability is revised at each reporting date and at settlement date, with changes in fair value recognised in profit or loss.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Long&#8209;term incentive plans</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The senior employees of Adevinta including the Adevinta executive management team were granted in June 2019 (with effect from 10 April 2019) a so&#8209;called Transition Award, LTI, SEP and the Adevinta Performance Share Plan (PSP).</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In May 2020, the Adevinta PSP for 2020 was granted to senior employees of Adevinta. In July 2021, the Adevinta PSP for 2021, Merger and New Joiner awards were granted to senior employees of Adevinta. In May 2022, the Adevinta PSP for 2022, Merger and New Joiner awards were granted to senior employees of Adevinta. During June to November 2021 the Legacy Equity Plan (LEP), DAVI Plan and Spot Equity awards were granted to key management and some employees of Adevinta in relation to the acquisition of eBay Classifieds Group. </font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">The Adevinta Performance Share Plan (&#8220;PSP&#8221;)</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">In June 2019 (with effect from 10 April 2019), in May 2020 (with effect from 1 January 2020), in July 2021 (with effect from 1 January 2021), and in May 2022 (with effect from 1 January 2022) the PSP was granted to senior employees of Adevinta including the Adevinta executive management team. Under the PSP, the employees will be granted awards of Adevinta ASA shares on an annual basis. These shares will be subject to a three&#8209;year vesting period (for the Adevinta executive management team the vesting is subject to an additional holding and employment period meaning that 50% of their awards vests after three years, 25% of their awards vests after four years and the remaining 25% of their awards vests after 5 years for the 2019 and 2020 awards and the 2021 and 2022 awards vest 100% after three years but are subject to a further two year holding requirement), at the end of which they will be transferred to the employee. Under the PSP, the employee will be granted an award over Adevinta ASA shares based on their prescribed maximum opportunity under the plan (for the Adevinta executive management team the maximum amount is in the range of 175% and 300% of his&#47;her base salary). The number of shares the employee receives will depend on the Adevinta ASA share price performance against a peer group (relative Total Shareholder Return (TSR)) over a three&#8209;year performance period. The payout mechanism related to the PSP is as follows&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; For minimum payout, Adevinta ASA shares must perform better than 50% of Adevinta ASA&#8217;s peers (&#8220;median&#8221; relative TSR). If this is achieved, 25% of the shares granted to the employees under the PSP award will be transferred to the employee after the performance period.</font></div><div style="height:52.56pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;text-align:right"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Roboto',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">32</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:73.44pt;width:100%"><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Adevinta ASA</font></div><div><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt"><font style="color:#1f1f1f;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">31 December 2022</font></div></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; For maximum payout, Adevinta ASA shares must perform better than 75% of Adevinta ASA&#8217;s peers (&#8220;upper quartile&#8221; relative TSR). If this is achieved, 100% of the shares granted to the employee under the PSP award will &#8220;vest&#8221; and be transferred to the employee.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8226; The payout is linear between the minimum and maximum payout.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The terms of the PSP Awards granted in 2020 and vested on 31 December 2022, were modified on 3 May 2022. Prior to the modification, the terms of awards were the same as for the 2022 Grant under the PSP (described above), with a TSR measurement period of 30 calendar days. For executives, EPSP Awards granted in 2020 are not subject to the EPSP Holding Period and 50% vested on 31 December 2022, 25% vest on 31 December 2023 and the final 25% vest on 31 December 2024, subject to the executive staying in employment with the Group (note that the TSR performance condition is measured with reference to the performance period to 31 December 2022 for all tranches). Pursuant to the modification, a minimum of 25% of the EPSP and NPSP Awards granted in May 2020 will vest. For TSR performance between median and upper-quartile, straight line vesting will apply from 25% vesting to 100% vesting as applied to the original award.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The fair value of shares granted has been estimated at the date of grant using a Monte&#8209;Carlo simulation model, taking into account the terms and conditions on which the share options have been granted. The model simulates the TSR and compares it against a group of peers. It takes into account the projection period, the share price (Adevinta ASA share price) at grant date, the risk&#8209;free interest rate, the dividend yield, the share price volatility of both Adevinta ASA and the peer group, future expected correlation of comparators&#8217; TSR and initial TSR performance.</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The peer group regarding the PSP is the group of companies in the STOXX Europe 600 Index (Europe&#8217;s 600 largest listed companies that are between half and twice the size of Adevinta ASA, as measured by market capitalisation at date of grant). The total fair value of the PSP granted in 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022 was estimated at the grant date to be &#8364;9 million, &#8364;4 million, &#8364;13 million and &#8364;1 million, respectively, which will be expensed over the vesting period subject to forfeiture.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Legacy equity plan (&#8220;LEP&#8221;)</font></div><div style="margin-top:5pt;padding-right:4.25pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">The LEP awards were granted on 6 August 2021 and will vest in installments as set out below. Awards under the LEP were issued to employees of eBay Classifieds Group as a voluntary replacement of the unvested awards previously issued by eBay (eCG&#8217;s former parent company), which lapsed and were forfeited as a result of Adevinta ASA&#8217;s acquisition of eBay Classifieds Group.</font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">LEP &#8211;
